I read the whole file (lines 1–190) and judged it only against the "Repeated proof machinery" rubric. I did not open any other source files, so this rests on the target file alone.

The proofs in the file are almost all short term-mode wrappers or `rfl`. This applies to `finiteLocallyFreeBicommutativeHopfAlgProperty_baseChange`, `baseChange`, `baseChangeMap`, `baseChangeFunctor_obj`, `baseChangeFunctor_map` and the two `baseChangeDualNatIso_*_app` lemmas. It also applies to `baseChangeDualIso` and `baseChangeDualIso_hom_apply_tmul_apply_tmul`, which each just apply an existing `ConvolutionDual` lemma.

Only two proofs have real tactic content:
- `baseChangeDualIso_hom_naturality` is `apply hom_ext` followed by an existing lemma.
- `baseChangeDualIso_inv_naturality` is derived from the hom version with a three-step `rw`.

The inverse proof reuses the hom lemma instead of repeating its argument. The `rw` is a routine isomorphism manipulation, so it is not nontrivial duplicated reasoning. Pulling it into a helper would only wrap existing `Iso` API.

I found no block of mathematical reasoning that appears in two proofs, so I report no finding.
